import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Calculate total spending across all product categories
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
df['TotalSpending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Drop rows with NaN in 'Income' or 'Education' as they are critical for this visualization
df.dropna(subset=['Income', 'Education'], inplace=True)

# Filter out extreme outliers in Income for better visualization of the main data cluster.
# Capping income at the 99th percentile helps prevent a few extreme values from distorting the plot.
income_cap = df['Income'].quantile(0.99)
df_filtered = df[df['Income'] <= income_cap].copy()

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes for the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a scatter plot of Total Spending vs. Income, colored by Education level
sns.scatterplot(data=df_filtered, x='Income', y='TotalSpending', hue='Education',
                palette='viridis', alpha=0.7, s=70, edgecolor='w', linewidth=0.5)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Total Customer Spending vs. Income by Education Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Income', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending on Products', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlapping with the plot
plt.legend(title='Education Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)

# Add a grid for better readability of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels and legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
